candidates.lesson_title: The Periodic Table and Its Groups
candidates.targets: Reactivity increases down Group 1 (easier to lose an electron) but decreases down Group 7 (harder to gain an electron) — the trends are opposite, not the same rule.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: periodic table (title), alkali metal (heading), group 1 (heading), group 7 (heading), halogen (heading), noble gas (heading); section overlap 0.50

candidates.lesson_title: Atoms, Elements, Compounds and the Model of the Atom
candidates.matched_section: The Development of the Atomic Model
candidates.targets: An atom is not a solid, densely packed ball, it consists of a tiny dense nucleus surrounded by mostly empty space occupied by electrons.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: model of the atom (title), alpha particle (body), bohr (body), gold foil (body), nucleus (body), plum pudding (body); section overlap 0.66

candidates.targets: Current is the same everywhere in a series circuit; it is energy/voltage that is shared out across components according to their resistance, not current disappearing.
candidates.why: built for science/electronics; keywords matched: current (title), parallel circuit (title), resistance (title), voltage (title), series circuit (heading), ammeter (body); section overlap 0.43

candidates.lesson_title: Conservation of Energy, Efficiency and Energy Resources
candidates.targets: Wasted thermal energy is transferred to the surroundings and becomes increasingly spread out (dispersed), but it still exists — it is not destroyed or lost from the universe.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: conservation of energy (title), efficiency (title), dissipation (heading), energy transfer (heading), energy store (body), thermal store (body); section overlap 0.48

candidates.targets: Forces in opposite directions subtract (vector combination) rather than just adding magnitudes together.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: resultant force (title), scalar (title), vector (title), free body diagram (heading), acceleration (body), balanced force (body); section overlap 0.32

candidates.lesson_title: Internal Energy, Specific Heat Capacity and Latent Heat
candidates.matched_section: Changes of State and Internal Energy
candidates.targets: During a change of state, energy continues to be absorbed/released (breaking/forming bonds) even though the thermometer reading stays flat.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: internal energy (title), latent heat (title), specific latent heat (title), boiling (body), change of state (body), heating curve (body); section overlap 0.54

candidates.targets: Fractional distillation separates hydrocarbons by differences in boiling point (vapour condensing at different heights/temperatures), not by physical sieving of molecule sizes.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: crude oil (title), fraction (title), fractional distillation (title), hydrocarbon (title), alkane (heading), boiling point (body); section overlap 0.65

candidates.lesson_title: Density, States of Matter and Changes of State
candidates.targets: During a change of state, energy continues to be absorbed/released (breaking/forming bonds) even though the thermometer reading stays flat.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: particle model (title), internal energy (heading), boiling (body), change of state (body), condensation (body), evaporation (body); section overlap 0.61

candidates.lesson_title: Trophic Levels and Transfer of Biomass
candidates.matched_section: How Is Biomass Lost Between Trophic Levels?
candidates.targets: Most biomass/energy loss between trophic levels is due to respiration (heat loss from movement/life processes), not simply parts of organisms being uneaten.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: biomass (title), food chain (title), trophic level (title), consumer (body), decomposer (body), ecosystem (body); section overlap 0.62

candidates.widget_name: Sealed flask: the next ten seconds
candidates.targets: At equilibrium, forward and reverse reactions both continue at equal rates simultaneously — the reaction hasn't stopped and concentrations need not be equal
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: dynamic equilibrium (title), equilibrium (title), reversible reaction (title), haber process (heading), closed system (body), forward reaction (body); section overlap 0.56

candidates.targets: In electrolysis, ions move because opposite charges attract at a distance, not because electrodes 'pull' ions or ions move randomly.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: electrolysis (title), ion (title), aqueous (heading), electrode (heading), half equation (heading), molten (heading); section overlap 0.54

candidates.widget_name: Which way do the electrons go?
candidates.lesson_title: Reactivity of Metals and Metal Extraction
candidates.anchor: Oxidation and Reduction in Terms of Electrons (Higher Tier)
candidates.targets: Displacement reactions occur because more reactive metals more readily lose electrons to less reactive metal ions — position in the reactivity series reflects and explains this electron-transfer tendency, not physical force or arbitrary memorisation.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: displacement (title), ore (title), reactivity series (title), extraction of metals (heading), oxidation (heading), reduction (heading); section overlap 0.44

candidates.targets: A single dominant allele is enough to prevent a recessive disorder showing, so a carrier (Ff) is unaffected despite carrying the recessive allele.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: allele (title), dominant (title), inheritance (title), recessive (title), cystic fibrosis (heading), carrier (body); section overlap 0.44

candidates.targets: Antibodies tag, clump or neutralise pathogens; phagocytes/other cells do the actual destroying.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: immune (title), infection (title), pathogen (title), antibiotic (body), antibodies (body), antibody (body); section overlap 0.50

candidates.targets: The seven regions of the EM spectrum are not fundamentally different things but a single continuous spectrum differing only in wavelength/frequency.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: electromagnetic spectrum (title), gamma ray (heading), infrared (heading), microwave (heading), radio wave (heading), ultraviolet (heading); section overlap 0.50

candidates.widget_name: Can it live on its surface alone?
candidates.targets: Surface area to volume ratio is a real physical constraint on diffusion rate, not just an abstract number, and explains why larger organisms need specialised exchange systems.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: transport (title), active transport (heading), diffusion (heading), osmosis (heading), exchange surface (body), gill (body); section overlap 0.44

candidates.targets: Antibodies tag, clump or neutralise pathogens; phagocytes/other cells do the actual destroying.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: antibiotic (title), immunity (title), vaccination (title), antibodies (body), antibody (body), antigen (body); section overlap 0.43

candidates.targets: When a C=C double bond opens during polymerisation, its electrons are used to form new single bonds with neighbouring carbons, not lost or 'broken off'.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: polymer (title), addition polymerisation (heading), alkene (body), double bond (body), ethene (body), monomer (body); section overlap 0.57

candidates.lesson_title: The Heart, Blood and Circulatory Disease
candidates.targets: The left and right sides of the heart contract simultaneously (not sequentially), pumping blood through two connected loops, with the left ventricle wall thicker to generate higher pressure for the systemic circuit.
candidates.why: built for science/pe; keywords matched: blood vessel (title), circulatory (title), heart (title), atrium (body), pulmonary (body), systemic (body); section overlap 0.33

candidates.lesson_title: Space Physics: The Solar System and Beyond
candidates.targets: Redshift arises because the wavelength of light is lengthened as the source recedes or as space expands, not because the light itself is being pulled or stretched like a rubber band by the galaxy.
candidates.why: built for astronomy/science; keywords matched: expanding universe (title), big bang (heading), red-shift (heading), cosmic microwave (body), doppler (body), galaxy (body); section overlap 0.51

candidates.targets: Multiple hormones (oestrogen, LH, FSH, progesterone) rise, fall, and trigger/suppress each other simultaneously through feedback loops, rather than acting in a simple day-by-day sequence.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: contraception (title), fsh (title), hormone (title), lh (title), menstrual cycle (title), oestrogen (title); section overlap 0.38

candidates.targets: Variation already exists before selection; organisms don't consciously try to adapt or gain traits because they are needed, and 'fittest' means best suited to environment, not strongest.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: evolution (title), natural selection (title), variation (title), mutation (heading), selective breeding (heading), darwin (body); section overlap 0.35

candidates.widget_name: How far does the signal get?
candidates.targets: At a synapse the electrical impulse triggers neurotransmitter release across the gap, which then generates a new electrical impulse in the next neuron, it does not simply jump across like a spark.
candidates.why: built for science/psychology; keywords matched: neuron (title), neurone (title), receptor (title), reflex arc (title), synapse (title), axon (body); section overlap 0.31

candidates.targets: A transformer that steps up voltage causes current to decrease proportionally, so power (and total energy) is conserved, not increased.
candidates.why: built for science/electronics; keywords matched: transformer (title), voltage (title), national grid (heading), step-down (heading), step-up (heading), power (body); section overlap 0.30

candidates.lesson_title: Rates of Reaction and Collision Theory
candidates.targets: Increasing temperature increases the proportion of particles with energy above the activation energy (shifting the distribution), which matters more than simply increasing collision frequency.
candidates.why: built for science; keywords matched: collision theory (title), catalyst (heading), concentration (heading), rate of reaction (heading), surface area (heading), temperature (heading); section overlap 0.41
